sentences.text: JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 14-02-2023 at about 4-30 p.m the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian towards Hoskote to K.R.Puram service road, when she reached near Katamnallur bus stop, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru driver of Car bearing registration No.KA-02/AG-2200 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner, as a result the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3.

It is further stated that immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Kempanna Hospital Hoskote, wherein she took conservative treatment inpatient and spent huge amount towards her medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment etc.,
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident she was working as Associate Admin at Brigade Mall, Kattamnallur cross, Hosakote and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
5.
It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-02/AG-2200.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Hoskote Traffic Police in Crime No.32/2023.
As such, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition,
seeking compensation.

6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal,
hence it was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 has stated that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further it has denied the entire case of the petitioner as false.
This respondent has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car bearing registration No.KA-02/AG-2200.
Further it is contended that, the driver of offending vehicle had not possessed the valid D.L. as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further it has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained by the petitioner, age, avocation and income of the petitioner as false.

It is also the contention of the Bhagyamma vs Sai Foods Pvt Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77170621/
2 respondent No.2 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, which took place on 14.02.2023 at about 4.30 pm near Katamnalluru bus station, Bidarahalli hobli, towards hoskote to K.R Puram service road, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AG-2200 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 and placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-02/AG- 2200, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the respondent No.2 though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
16. The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
PW1 in her examination- in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P8.

Ex. P1- copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of vehicle seizure mahazar, Ex.P6- true copy of IMV report, Ex.P7- true copy of MLC, Ex.P8-true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P9 & Ex.P10-copies of notice issued to witnesses and Ex.P11-true copy of the charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Hosakote police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

18. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
19. Though the respondent No.2 contended that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
But in this regard respondent No.2 has not examined either the driver of offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to the incident.

20. In the light of evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-02-AG-2200.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

sentences.text: Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

Pain and Sufferings;
23.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P8.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-
Pain and swelling present over right knee joint X-ray shows right knee joint--
No gross fractures seen MRI right knee shows high grade tear of ACL vertical tear involving anterior horn of lateral meciscus with associated T2/PDFS Hyperdensities grade III meniscal injury.
24. In connection with the above said injury, the doctor is of the opinion that said injury is grievous in nature.
The petitioner has placed x-ray, CT scan and MRI at Ex.P15 to Ex.P17.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2.
PW2 has stted in his evidence that the petitiner has sustained ACL tear with Meniscal injury right knee.
She was treated conservatively.
PW2 has placed OPD and MRI at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an inpatient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
25.
PW1 has stated that, she was working as as a Associate (Admin) and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In support of her case, she has placed pay slips at Ex.P13.
On perusal of pay slip for the month of January 2023 marked at Ex.P13 the petitioner was getting salary of Rs.18,530/- per month.

sentences.text: deducting Rs.200/- professional tax, it comes to Rs.18,330/- per month.
Further PW1 has stated that due to the accidental injuries she took four months leave.
But she has not placed any documents to show that due to the accidental injuries she had applied four months leave.
As per inpatient record marked at Ex.P14 petitioner took the treatment from 15.2.2023 to 15.2.2023.

As the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.

Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.36,660/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills as per Ex.P14 to the extent of Rs.20,770/-.
There are no any contradictions to disbelieve the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for medical bills of Rs.20,770/- and same is awarded towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.
As per the medical records and also on going through the inpatient record the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for one day.
During that period, definitely the petitioner might have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained by the petitoner, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
28.
The petitioner herein asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by her as per Ex.P8 goes to show that, she had sustained grievous injury, for which she took the treatment as inpatient for one day.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained ACL tear with menscal injury right knee.

On examination walks with pain and limping,
wasting of right lower limb is seen, anterior drawer's test and MC Murray's test for medial Meniscus is positive.
MRI shows partial ACL tear, Grade 1 lateral meniscal tear and lateral patellar retinaculum tear.
Further he has assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 30% and whole body disability at 15%.

He has placed outpatient record and MRI scan, which are marked at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.
29.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not treated doctor.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.

sentences.text: PW1 has stated that she was working as a Associate (Admin) and was drawing salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
She has placed pay slip for the month of January 2023, which is marked at Ex.P13.
On perusal of pay slip marked at Ex.P13 the petitioner was getting salary of Rs.18,530/- per month.
After deducting professional tax of Rs.200/- it comes to Rs.18,330/- per month.
In the cross examination she has stated that she had applied leave for four months.
Now she is not getting salary as she removed from her service.
But she has not placed any document to show that due to the accidental injuries she removed from her service.
Hence, it has to be considered she has continued her service as usual.
31. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.
At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to her to do normal work, as she was earlier.

Hence, I relied the decision reported in, ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, it was observed,
that.

entities.text: Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.
The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

32. On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

33. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued her job, she has to suffer with the said disability throughout her life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.

sentences.text: As noted above, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident as a result she has permanent partial disability.
The petitioner was aged about 32 years at the time of the accident.

The said disability certainly affects not only on her avocation, but also affects on her amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy her life as she was enjoying earlier prior to the accident.
By overall considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities.
35. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that the petitioner has to undergo surgery in the form of ACL reconstruction, which would cost around Rs.50,000/-.
Replying on the opinion of the doctor, it is proper to award Rs.20,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Sl. Compensation heads Compensation No. Amount 1 Pain and Suffering Rs.
30,000-00 2 Loss of income during laid- Rs. 36,660-00 up period and rest period 3 Medical expenses Rs. 20,770-00 4 Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 5,000-00 Conveyance Charges 5. Reduced disability of Rs. 50,000-00 employment 5 Loss of Amenities Rs.
10,000-00 6 Future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.1,72,430-00 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,430/- (Rupees one lakh seventy two thousand four hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.KA-02-AG-2200 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
39. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 19.08.2022 to 18.8.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 14.2.2023.
Therefore, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
40.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,430/- (Rupees one lakh seventy two thousand four hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

In view of valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
39. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 19.08.2022 to 18.8.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 14.2.2023.
Therefore, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.

opennyai_summary.decision:
By overall considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Replying on the opinion of the doctor, it is proper to award Rs.20,000/- under the head future medical expenses.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,430/- (Rupees one lakh seventy two thousand four hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,430/- (Rupees one lakh seventy two thousand four hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
In view of valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
